visual_leaf_symptoms: Oldest bottom leaves turn pale yellow while top leaves remain light green
Veins on lower leaves may show yellowing that spreads across the entire leaf blade
deficiencies.biological_reason: Nitrogen is mobile in plants; when starved, the plant cannibalizes nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed new top shoots.

diy_remedy.name: Stinging Nettle or Green Weed Ferment (Survivor Liquid Gold)
diy_remedy.recipe: Pack a bucket half-full with crushed fresh stinging nettles, young comfrey, or leafy green weeds. Fill to the brim with rainwater. Cover loosely with a flat stone and let steep in the sun for 7 to 10 sun cycles until it turns dark, bubbly, and smells pungent.
diy_remedy.application: Dilute 1 part dark weed tea with 5 parts clean water. Pour one cup around the base of each heavy feeder crop once every 4 suns.

alternative_remedy.name: The Golden Water Tonic (Diluted Camp Urine)
alternative_remedy.recipe: Fresh human urine is sterile in healthy survivors and extremely rich in pure urea nitrogen. Dilute 1 cup fresh urine into 10 cups clean water.
alternative_remedy.application: Pour directly onto the root zone soil around corn, squash, and brassicas. Avoid wetting edible leaves directly.

visual_leaf_symptoms: Leaves take on a distinct dark green, purplish, or bronzed hue, especially along veins and leaf undersides
Flowering and fruiting are delayed; root systems remain tiny and weak
deficiencies.biological_reason: Phosphorus is required for cellular energy (ATP) and root branching. Stunted transport causes purple anthocyanin pigment buildup.

diy_remedy.name: Campfire Bone Meal (White Gold)
diy_remedy.recipe: Gather leftover animal bones from camp stews. Roast them in hot campfire coals until they turn chalky gray and brittle. Crush them between two flat stones into a coarse white powder.
diy_remedy.application: Sprinkle two generous handfuls around the root zone of fruiting plants (tomatoes, squash, beans) and work into the top finger-depth of soil before watering.

alternative_remedy.name: Decaying Forest Pond Silt
alternative_remedy.recipe: Scoop dark black silt from the bed of a slow-moving forest stream or pond edge where fish, leaves, and aquatic organisms have decayed for years.
alternative_remedy.application: Top-dress one bucketful around plant roots per bed pace.

visual_leaf_symptoms: Margins and tips of older leaves turn brown, curled, and brittle ('scorched' edges) while the center remains green
Stems are weak, floppy, and vulnerable to snapping in wind
Fruits are small, unevenly ripened, or bland in taste
deficiencies.biological_reason: Potassium regulates cellular water pressure (stomata) and enzyme synthesis. Deficiency causes leaf edges to dry and scorch.

diy_remedy.name: Cold Hardwood Ash Tea
diy_remedy.recipe: Scoop two handfuls of cold, clean gray wood ash from campfire coals (hardwood is best: oak, maple, fruit woods; avoid burned plastics or treated wood). Stir into a bucket of water and let sit overnight until the powder settles.
diy_remedy.application: Pour the clear water gently at the base of plants. Ash tea is naturally rich in soluble potassium and calcium. Apply once every 10 suns.

alternative_remedy.name: Comfrey Leaf Mulch Blanket
alternative_remedy.recipe: Comfrey has deep taproots that mine subsoil potassium. Cut broad leaves and lay them two fingers thick directly under fruiting plants as a decomposing blanket.
alternative_remedy.application: Decomposes rapidly, releasing potassium directly into top roots.

visual_leaf_symptoms: Youngest growing tips and newest leaves emerge curled, hook-shaped, or distorted
Blossom-end rot: the bottom blossom end of developing tomatoes or squash turns black, sunken, and leathery
Buds abort and fall off before opening
deficiencies.biological_reason: Calcium forms cell wall bonds. Unlike nitrogen, calcium cannot move from old leaves to new ones; irregular watering causes dry tip collapse.

diy_remedy.name: Camp Vinegar & Shell Fizz Solution
diy_remedy.recipe: Collect eggshells, mussel shells, or land snail shells. Crush into tiny fragments. Place a handful into a jar and cover with wild vinegar (or sour fermented fruit mash). Watch it fizz vigorously as calcium carbonate dissolves into water-soluble calcium acetate.
diy_remedy.application: Dilute half a cup of the clear strained liquid into a bucket of rainwater. Drench soil around fruiting vegetables.

alternative_remedy.name: Even Moisture Mulching
alternative_remedy.recipe: Calcium starvation is frequently caused by soil drying out between rains, preventing roots from absorbing calcium. Pack a hand-deep mulch of dry leaves or straw to maintain constant soil dampness.
alternative_remedy.application: Maintains smooth sap flow to developing fruits.
